artifact.working_title: August 2026 multi-pathogen alfalfa sprout outbreak: 55 cases, Everything Sprouts recall
conversation_questions: How should a multi-pathogen sprout outbreak be described without implying more about the contamination source than traceback currently shows?
What is the most useful consumer takeaway when lot codes may be missing, product was frozen without packaging, or sprouts were eaten at a restaurant?
How much, if any, weight belongs on AP’s prior-year warning-letter reporting versus the current epidemiologic and traceback link?
How should 15-state case reports be discussed alongside FDA’s confirmed recalled-product distribution only in Minnesota and Wisconsin so far?
What, if anything, changes about the public-health story because two people were infected with both Salmonella and STEC?
Which caveats should stay attached to every number: undercount, 3–4 week reporting lag, and an ongoing inspection?
uncertainties_and_open_checks: Fact-check guardrail: case counts, onset dates, hospitalization figures, and the distribution map can change because FDA and CDC say the investigation is ongoing.
Investigators have not established the contamination source (for example grower conditions versus a common seed supplier).
FDA has not finished determining whether additional products, lots, firms, or states are linked.
Confirmed recalled-product distribution is MN and WI, while illnesses are reported from 15 states; further movement of product is still being checked.
CDC says the true number of illnesses is likely much higher and recent cases may not yet be counted.
AP reported, earlier, that the company had not yet issued a recall; the later FDA advisory says a recall began August 22. Use the FDA chronology and do not treat the AP line as current recall status.
AP said it had not obtained comment from Everything Sprouts.
WGS-predicted Salmonella resistance is described as unlikely to change treatment for most people; it is not, on this record, a demonstrated treatment-failure finding.

what_happened.text: As of FDA’s August 24, 2026 update, FDA and CDC are investigating a multistate outbreak of STEC (O26:H11, O103:H25, O168:H8) and Salmonella Agona. Epidemiologic and traceback data identify alfalfa sprouts from Everything Sprouts, LLC, Minneapolis, as a source. 55 people from 15 states: 46 E. coli, 7 Salmonella, 2 both; 4 hospitalizations; 0 deaths; onsets May 31–August 8, 2026. Of 34 people interviewed, 26 (76%) ate alfalfa sprouts. On August 22 the firm recalled Calco and Everything Sprouts 5-oz alfalfa sprouts lots 222, 223, 225, 226, and 230, plus Crunchy Protein Sprout Mix lots 222, 223, 226, 230 and Zesty Garlic Mix lots 222, 223, 225, 226, 230. Product went to wholesale, grocery, and restaurants in MN and WI from May 27–August 21, 2026. FDA inspected and sampled starting August 19. Investigation ongoing.

why_it_matters_now.text: Public guidance is active: do not eat, sell, or serve recalled Calco/Everything Sprouts alfalfa sprouts or the named mix cups; throw away or return them, including unmarked frozen leftovers; clean surfaces they touched; seek care for STEC- or Salmonella-like symptoms after exposure. CDC notes a 3–4 week lag in linking cases and says the true number sick is likely higher. Labeled inference: this is still a live consumer-alert story because distribution beyond MN/WI is not closed, restaurant exposure occurred, and additional products or firms have not been ruled in or out.

verified_facts.text: Current published tally: 55 illnesses, 4 hospitalizations, 0 deaths, 15 states. Illness onsets May 31 to August 8, 2026.
Pathogens named: STEC O26:H11, O103:H25, and O168:H8, plus Salmonella Agona. Some people had more than one outbreak strain.

Implicated grower/products: Everything Sprouts alfalfa sprouts sold as Calco and Everything Sprouts 5-oz cups (lots 222, 223, 225, 226, 230), also used in Crunchy Protein Sprout Mix and Zesty Garlic Mix cups with the listed lots. Recall initiated August 22, 2026.

Confirmed recalled-product distribution: wholesale distributors and grocery stores in Minnesota and Wisconsin, and restaurants in those states, May 27–August 21, 2026. FDA is checking whether product went farther. Recalled restaurant product should no longer be for sale.

AP lists additional states with reported cases: Florida, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, New Hampshire, New York, Pennsylvania, North Carolina, South Carolina, North Dakota, South Dakota, and Washington, after state officials described more than three dozen cases in Minnesota and Wisconsin.

Among 55 people with age/sex data: ages 12–94, median 34; 73% female. CDC: of 34 interviewed, 26 (76%) ate alfalfa sprouts, versus 8.7% reporting any sprouts in the FoodNet Population Survey. At least two illness clusters in Minnesota and Wisconsin.

WGS found outbreak isolates closely related. Salmonella from 9 people’s samples was predicted resistant to three or more of fosfomycin, streptomycin, sulfisoxazole, and tetracycline; CDC says this is unlikely to change treatment for most people. STEC from 46 samples had no predicted resistance; antibiotics are not recommended for STEC.

tension_or_argument.text: Established tension: foodborne outbreaks are usually defined by one germ; this one involves Salmonella plus multiple STEC serotypes, including two dual infections. A second tension is clock/status: AP, citing FDA at the time of its story, said the company had not yet issued a recall; FDA’s August 24 advisory says Everything Sprouts initiated a recall on August 22. Labeled inference/context only: AP’s report that FDA sent a warning letter the previous year over a leaking roof dripping onto bean sprouts and workers’ smocks is background about the firm, not evidence that those conditions caused this outbreak.

surprising_details.text: Two people were infected with both Salmonella and E. coli outbreak strains.
Sprout exposure among interviewees (76%) far exceeded the 8.7% FoodNet baseline for any sprouts.
The same alfalfa sprouts were packed not only as plain 5-oz cups but also into Crunchy Protein Sprout Mix and Zesty Garlic Mix cups.
Last reported illness onset is August 8, while recalled product was still being distributed through August 21.
WGS predicted multidrug resistance in Salmonella from 9 samples, while STEC isolates had no predicted resistance.

flexible_outline.text: Neutral top line from established evidence only: 55 illnesses in 15 states, four hospitalizations, no deaths, STEC plus Salmonella Agona, linked to Everything Sprouts alfalfa sprouts; recall of named Calco/Everything Sprouts lots; investigation ongoing. Flag that counts and maps can move.

Concise chronology: onsets May 31–August 8; distribution May 27–August 21; FDA inspection/sampling August 19; August 21 outbreak advisory; August 22 firm-initiated recall; August 24 FDA update. Keep AP’s earlier ‘no recall yet’ line as a superseded status report, not the current fact.

Why multiple pathogens matter (descriptive, not causal speculation) and practical guidance: do not eat/sell/serve recalled lots; discard unmarked frozen product; clean contact surfaces; who is at higher Salmonella risk; STEC/HUS warning and when to seek care.
Supporting epi only: 76% sprout exposure vs FoodNet 8.7%; at least two MN/WI clusters; demographics (median age 34, 73% female); WGS relatedness and the limited resistance findings.
Labeled inference/context, if used at all: AP warning-letter/roof item as prior regulatory background, explicitly not proof of this contamination pathway.
Cut first if comparing stories: extra state names, mix-cup lot lists, restaurant-versus-grocery distribution detail, and PulseNet/WGS method explanation.

Close on open checks: contamination source unknown; possible additional firms/seeds/states; undercount and reporting lag. Source note: FDA advisory, AP story, CDC investigation update. Archive search found no relevant prior Nonsense sprout-outbreak coverage.
